rules.name: APP Fraud Mandatory Reimbursement
rules.source_legislation: PSR APP Fraud Reimbursement Policy (PS23/3); Payment Systems Act 2013; FPS Scheme Rules (Pay.UK)
rules.description: From 7 October 2024, the bank as a PSP must reimburse victims of Authorised Push Payment (APP) fraud up to £85,000 per claim. Reimbursement must be made to the sending customer within 5 business days of a claim being submitted unless a stop-the-clock provision applies. The total reimbursement cost is split 50/50 between the sending PSP and the receiving PSP. The scheme is funded by a per-transaction levy on FPS payments. The bank must maintain a claims decisioning process, a reimbursement reserve, and a fraud reporting process to the PSR.
disclosure_obligations: Customer-facing APP fraud reimbursement policy published on the bank's website
Reimbursement claim outcome letter to customer within 5 business days
Quarterly claims and reimbursement data submitted to PSR for monitoring
Annual disclosure of APP fraud volumes and reimbursement rates to PSR
constraints: Reimbursement must be paid within 5 business days unless stop-the-clock applies (e.g. suspected gross negligence investigation)
Gross negligence standard applies — reimbursement may be refused only if customer ignored PSP warnings or acted fraudulently
The FPS transaction levy funding the scheme cannot be directly passed on to retail customers

rules.name: Confirmation of Payee (CoP) — Phase 2 Mandatory Coverage
rules.source_legislation: PSR Specific Direction 17 (SD17); PSR Group 2 participation mandatory from October 2024
rules.description: The bank must perform Confirmation of Payee checks on all outbound FPS and CHAPS payments, verifying the payee name against the account held at the receiving bank. Outbound payments where CoP returns a 'no match' or 'partial match' result must be presented to the customer with a prominent risk warning and confirmation step before the payment is allowed to proceed. The bank must also respond to inbound CoP requests from other PSPs within the scheme latency requirements.
disclosure_obligations: CoP check result presented to customer before payment authorisation in a standardised format
No-match and partial-match results accompanied by explicit fraud risk warning
Confirmation of Payee coverage rate reported to PSR annually
constraints: CoP must be performed on 100% of outbound FPS and CHAPS payments — no blanket exemptions
Inbound CoP request response must be returned within the scheme's latency SLA
Customer must actively confirm intent to proceed when CoP returns no-match — passive timeout is not acceptable

rules.name: CHAPS ISO 20022 Enhanced Data — Structured Addresses and LEIs
rules.source_legislation: Bank of England CHAPS ISO 20022 Enhanced Data Policy; RTGS/CHAPS Rules
rules.description: From 1 May 2025, all CHAPS payments must include LEIs (Legal Entity Identifiers) for corporate originators and beneficiaries and Purpose Codes for specified transaction categories. From November 2026, unstructured postal addresses in CHAPS messages will be rejected; banks must migrate to structured address formats across all onboarding, channels, and payment processing systems. The bank must implement address enrichment processes and LEI validation as part of CHAPS payment origination.
disclosure_obligations: LEI population rate reported to Bank of England as part of CHAPS data quality audit programme
Internal programme plan for structured address migration shared with Bank of England relationship manager
Board-level sign-off on structured address migration readiness by Q3 2026
constraints: LEIs and Purpose Codes mandatory in all in-scope CHAPS messages from 1 May 2025
Unstructured postal addresses rejected by CHAPS central infrastructure from November 2026
LEI validation must occur at payment origination — invalid or expired LEIs must be flagged and remediated before submission

rules.name: RTGS Extended Operating Hours — Settlement Window Management
rules.source_legislation: Bank of England RTGS Extended Operating Hours policy statement (expected 2025–2026); CHAPS Rules
rules.description: The Bank of England is targeting a 01:30 opening of RTGS settlement by end-2025 and is consulting on evening and bank holiday settlement, with near-continuous settlement as an end-of-decade aspiration. The bank must update its CHAPS settlement position monitoring, intraday liquidity management, and operational staffing to cover the extended settlement window. Treasury must maintain adequate settlement reserves across the expanded hours.
disclosure_obligations: Updated CHAPS participation terms acknowledging extended operating hours obligations
Client-facing communication updating CHAPS payment cutoff times as extended hours are adopted
Internal operational readiness attestation submitted to Bank of England by agreed milestone
constraints: Bank must be operationally capable of processing CHAPS payments during the extended settlement window from the date of implementation
Intraday liquidity buffers must be maintained throughout the extended operating hours
Staffing and on-call arrangements must cover the full operational window

rules.name: Commercial Variable Recurring Payments (cVRP) — Scheme Participation
rules.source_legislation: FCA cVRP Scheme (announced 2024); PSR Variable Recurring Payments framework; PSR 2017
rules.description: Commercial VRP (cVRP) enables consumers and businesses to give pre-authorised payment mandates to third-party PISPs for subscription and variable recurring use cases beyond sweeping. The FCA-led scheme expects first live payments in Q1 2026. The bank as ASPSP must support cVRP consent grant, management, and revocation APIs, and must ensure its digital channel surfaces cVRP mandate management to customers. This creates a new open banking payment rail that competes directly with card recurring mandates and BACS direct debits.
approval_chain: Head of Open Banking and APIs
disclosure_obligations: cVRP mandate dashboard accessible to customers in online and mobile banking
Customer notification upon creation, modification, or revocation of a cVRP mandate
Scheme participation reporting to FCA/PSR per cVRP scheme rules
constraints: Bank must provide cVRP APIs meeting FCA scheme technical standards from scheme go-live
Customers must be able to revoke cVRP mandates instantly via digital channel
Payment limits and merchant restrictions agreed in the cVRP mandate must be enforced by the bank at execution

rules.name: Interbank Infrastructure Renewal (IIR) — Programme Participation
rules.source_legislation: HM Treasury Payments Forward Plan (26 February 2026); Payments Vision Delivery Committee roadmap 2026–2028
rules.description: HM Treasury's Payments Forward Plan formally replaced the New Payments Architecture (NPA) with the Interbank Infrastructure Renewal (IIR) programme, led by a new industry-governed Delivery Company. The bank must participate in IIR design and migration activities as a direct scheme participant. The three-year regulatory roadmap (2026–2028) covers migration of domestic interbank rails to new infrastructure. The bank must appoint a senior IIR programme owner and provide resource to industry working groups.
disclosure_obligations: Annual IIR programme progress report to the Board
Participation in IIR Delivery Company governance as a direct participant
Regulatory reporting to PSR and Pay.UK on IIR migration readiness milestones
constraints: Bank must maintain active participation in IIR Delivery Company governance and technical working groups
Migration to new IIR infrastructure is mandatory within the PSR/Pay.UK timeline
Legacy FPS/BACS infrastructure investment must be balanced against IIR migration capex
